key_insight: Agentic Critical Training shifts agent learning from pure imitation to contrastive self-critique: agents are trained not only to copy expert actions but to generate, compare, and learn from suboptimal alternatives so they understand why actions succeed or fail.
problem_solved: Imitation learning teaches what to do but not why; agents lack awareness of action quality because they never contrast expert decisions with plausible alternatives, leading to brittle or suboptimal autonomous behavior.
method: Have the agent produce candidate actions (expert-like and alternative/suboptimal options) during training and collect pairwise comparisons.
Introduce a critic/contrastive supervision signal that scores and ranks alternatives so the agent learns to prefer high-quality actions and explain their advantage.
Train the policy with a contrastive or ranking objective that combines imitation of good actions with explicit penalties for suboptimal alternatives, closing the gap between 'what' and 'why'.
impact: By giving agents an explicit sense of action quality, this approach improves robustness, decision transparency, and downstream performance for autonomous LLM agents—especially in tasks requiring long-horizon planning or error recovery.
visual_elements: Training loop diagram showing agent generating multiple action candidates, critic scoring them, and feedback updating the policy.
Before vs after panel: decisions made by imitation-only agent vs agent trained with critical contrasts, highlighting fewer failures.
Contrastive ranking chart that visualizes score distributions for expert vs alternative actions.
Icon set: agent, magnifying glass/critic, ranked list, and upward performance arrow to convey core concepts at a glance.
paper_authors: Weize Liu, Minghui Liu, Sy-Tuyen Ho, Souradip Chakraborty, Xiyao Wang
